title: Sending George Washington home from the Ma Rainey troupe
summary: Humphrey recounts helping trombonist George Washington leave Ma Rainey's stranded show and his later death; Washington came up with Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And I, the man was in the place, Cameron. I called him on the side, I said, man, I get about $75. What you gonna do with the money? I said, well, one of my good friends right there stranded. I'm gonna send him home. Who is that friend? When he come over the station, he didn't know George Washington. Little bit of fella played trombone. Good trombone player. I introduced him to Ma Rainey and George Washington and the whole cast sitting up there waiting for a telegram. Come from Baton Rouge somewhere to pull him into Baton Rouge. I wasn't gonna tell them that, you know. And I said George, $50. Well, his grandmother, his aunt was living down Thaddeus Street then. He said, well, I guess the next thing's smoking. All of them sitting up there asleep. He got out from there. Come on in the order. Mm-hmm. Poor little fella died. He was waking a long time, probably in the canal up there. Remember in, uh, Sonny Henry? That was J.J. dance too. Sidney Correa. All work up there. When I left here, that's where he was waking.
Well, when he died, he stayed on Washington near Jackson. On Washington near Jackson?

George Washington. One of these times. Now he, he and Louis Armstrong come up together back there in the Joneses home. He could play a baritone, bass on, and trombone. Mm-hmm. And he was good. See, I don't see nothing in that book. You know, I'll show you that book I have. No. I got a book of, you know, old musicians.
